title: S18 band-gap audit: 4.77M zeros missing from the exact tail; part-0 verdicts void; mechanism is K-overflow (resid=inf); local fix + mpmath thread-safety defect
body: Owner directive 'check the output for flaws before trusting the long run' paid off within hours of launch. S18's part-0 row output (tmp/s18_run.log, tmp/s18_S1marg_repair.jsonl) is VOID. Corrupted values: 3.1e7 and 3.75e7 all-24-rows margin = 0.000000 with resid = **inf** and E = -1.79642e+07 (i.e. Re(log K) = +1.796e7: K overflowed at dps-30); 5e7 rows 0.005-0.37 and 7.5e7 rows 0.009-0.51 (resid finite but huge). ROOT CAUSE: band-coverage gap in the 'exact' (3e7, 3e10] tail assembly. The tail = td cache (1e7, 3e7] (day023_taildiscrete LO,HI = 1e7,3e7; 47,517,736 zeros, structure re-verified) + streamed H1 files A/B/C/D, but file A (scripts/rh/hi1e9/zeros_hi31946e6_to_1e9.f64) starts at 31,946,000.0666, so the band (3e7, 31,945,999.623] = 4,772,897 zeros was in NEITHER half. Mechanism: re_stub (the missing near-diagonal zeros at t = 3.1e7) ~ -1.8e7, so K_corrupted = K_fixed * e^{+1.8e7} overflows mpf -> resid = |z - inf| = inf -> margin = |z|*dev/(B+inf) = 0. At 5e7/7.5e7 the stub effect is smaller (band further from t) so K overflowed only to finite-large values, giving the small-but-nonzero margins. WHY THE ARBITER MISSED IT: the launch closed-form vs stream check shares the same (3e7, 3e10] band assumption (internal consistency != band coverage). LESSON: band-coverage audits must read actual first/last zeros of each file, not docstring boundaries. THE DATA IS LOCAL: the LMFDB shard scripts/rh/lshards/zeros_29846000.dat (md5 55aa99035a99f522538af17b7900729e, identical to /tmp/zeta-dl/shards copy) covers (29,846,000.12, 31,945,999.6230] with perfect local structure (3000 consecutive zeros span ~1220-1225 units, min_gap > 0, production-style decode v = t0 + Z*2^-101). Seam verified at dps-40 by Rieman Xi real-line scan: shard last zero = 31,945,999.6229975, next zero = 31,946,000.06657648 = A[0] (agrees with the f64-file value to 2.3e-9, ~half ulp). The (1e7, 3e10] H1 tiling is therefore PERFECT except exactly the S18 assembly gap. FIX (no code change to S18, no recomputation): stub array tmp/s18_stub_zeros.f64 (4,772,897 zeros, production-style shard decode, tmp/shard11_fulltile.npy intermediate); the reissue script tmp/sx1f_s18b_reissue_part0.py extends td._G_CACHE with the stub before calling the UNMODIFIED s18.margin_at (its (1e7,3e7] term reads td._G_CACHE directly); the part-0 stream cache (tmp/s18_stream_part0_b4f11b3edbd520da.npz) is reused as-is (the A-D stream sums themselves were verified correct at launch); part-0 rows reissued single-threaded. SECOND DEFECT (harness, also found by the audit): mpmath is NOT thread-safe under concurrent shared-context dps-30 use: an 8-worker row phase produced a corrupted zeta value (14,029,948.27 at (3.1e7, k=-12) vs 1.4834 single-threaded - |zeta(1/2+it)| ~ 1e7 is impossible) plus intermittent ZeroDivisionError inside M.R_closed (den read as exact 0; single-thread deterministic). ALL margin evaluations are now serialized; the original S18 12-worker row phase is suspect for its zeta/dev auxiliary values (its margin=0 verdicts stand on the deterministic resid=inf, but everything should be reissued single-threaded). PROVENANCE NOTE: the day-023 'exp' baseline margins quoted in the S18 md template (0.7763 / 0.6609 / 0.3665 / 0.5257) do NOT reproduce today: re-running the UNMODIFIED day-023 density-quad composite on the recorded row (g=31,000,000, k=+3, t=31,000,001.5) gives margin 0.0000, resid inf, E = -4095.70 while zeta = 14.4743, dev = 1.0000, B = 5.30543 match the recorded row exactly (tmp/sx1g_day023_repro.log). The 2026-09-14 git history (commit 097ccbc) already declared rows above 3.15e7 'not certifiable (density quad cannot resolve zeros near t; needs actual zeros = data ask)'. Those exp numbers were pre-repair exploratory artifacts of the density tail, not certified baselines - they must not be used to judge the repair. RELIABILITY OF THE FIXED ROWS: the only modeled region left is the dps-30 density quad over (3e10, 1e18]; its per-zero weight t^2/g^2 is suppressed there (per-zero mismatch ~1e-6 at g=3e10), so its O(1) model error bounds K to a relative e^{O(1)} factor - adequate for a >=1 vs <1 verdict, not for sub-sigma claims. STATE: S18 part-1 A-D stream (targets 1e8..2.9e10) is valid/reusable data; part-1 D still streaming; single-threaded part-0 reissue running (96 rows). No RH claim in any direction; data-pipeline audit only.
